findings.what: At about 230 words in eight rows it is far over the 90-word limit for a SHOW screen, so fold Chatters into Wrong coil and Lost line into Overload trips, cut the repeated 'The overload also guards against a lost line', or move the coil faults to a screen of their own.

findings.where: Screen 2, The starter, live (the words around the picture)
findings.what: About 230 words sit round the picture: the prompt, the live sentence, a 39-word paragraph that repeats screen 1, three grey notes of about 130 words and a caption below Continue, so cut the repeat and merge the notes into one short 'Example values' line naming the showroom motor, the 7 times surge over 4 s and the sped-up overload.

findings.where: Screen 5, Where it is used, and its limits
findings.what: At about 170 words in six rows it is well over 90, so move 'More than one place to control it' to the faults screen or Keep this, drop 'Frequent starts' (screen 7 already says it), and give the size rules in one line such as 'Rules of thumb run from 4 to 5.5 kW.'

At about 135 words it is over 90, so cut 'That is well above rated torque, not equal to it.', which argues with a claim he never sees on this screen, and cut the contactor and quick-restart rows to one sentence each.
At about 120 words it is over 90, so keep the why and the showroom numbers and say the kit, the light-load rule and the second peak at the switch in two short sentences.
At about 115 words it is over 90, so drop 'The coil (4) is fed by a small control circuit.' and join 'The latching contact closes at the same moment' with the sentence after it.

findings.where: Screen 7, the Chatters or buzzes row
findings.what: 'Measure the coil voltage while it pulls in' is a live test, and it comes straight after 'Isolate and lock off' without saying so, so add one short sentence saying it is a live test, done with proper test probes on the coil terminals, and that he isolates again before touching anything.

findings.where: Screen 6, Star-delta, 'The torque falls further, to about a quarter'
findings.what: 'Further' hints at a reason that never comes, because by the voltage rule the torque falls to a third like the current, so say plainly that in practice it falls to about a quarter of a DOL start.

findings.where: Keep this card, screen 7 Overload trips row, and the practice worked example (27.70 A)
findings.what: 'Trips at 1.2 ×' reads as an instant trip at 27.7 A, though screen 2's note says a real overload takes far longer, so add 'slowly, on its trip curve' where the 1.2 × is given.

findings.where: Screen 2, the caption under Continue and the overload model
findings.what: The caption sits outside the card below Continue where it is easily missed, and because the start surge never heats the bar, repeated starts never trip the picture's overload even though screens 5 and 7 say they do, so let the surge heat the bar or move the caption into the example-values note.

findings.where: Screen 2, the read sentence for the read-through and the Book
findings.what: 'Let go, and the coil stays fed through 7' is an instruction in a read-through, and 'about 162 A' does not say it is the example motor with an example 7 times surge, so write 'When Start is let go, the coil stays fed through 7' and 'On the example motor the meter jumps to about 162 A'.

findings.where: Screen 2, the grey note on the overload
findings.what: 'About 6 s at 150%' comes from a heating rule that is never shown, so drop the figure or say 'much faster at 150%'.

findings.where: Screen 2, the prompt above the picture
findings.what: 'Then try Stop, the overload and a supply cut' points to an overload with no button, so say 'push the motor current up until the overload trips'.

findings.where: Screens 1 to 2, the drawing under the overload heaters (9)
findings.what: The heat bar is drawn across all three motor leads, so it looks like a link or terminal block joining L1 to L3, and nothing in the drawing ties 9 to 10, so move the bar beside 9, off the conductors, and add a dashed link from 9 to 10.

findings.where: Screen 2 at 360 px, the first button row
findings.what: 'Open isolator (2)' wraps onto three lines beside the one-line Start and Stop buttons, so shorten it to 'Isolator (2)' or give it a row of its own.

findings.where: Keep this card at 1280 px, the rule lines
findings.what: 'trips at 1.2 ×.' breaks so that '×.' sits alone on the next line, and 'over 10.' splits the same way, so use a no-break space before × and inside 'over 10'.
'For a small motor' leaves 'small' undefined, though the figure is for motors up to about 30 kW, so say that.
'1 ÷ √3 × 1 ÷ √3' is hard to read at a glance, so write '(1 ÷ √3) × (1 ÷ √3) = 1 ÷ 3'.

In 'It can also overheat' the 'It' could be the coil or the motor, and 0.575 is not tied to the 0.85 to 1.1 band in the row above, so write 'That coil can also overheat' and say that 0.575 is far below the 0.85 it needs.

A starter switched by a float or pressure switch instead of a Start button does restart by itself when the supply returns, which the low-voltage release source already covers, so one sentence would stop him applying no-volt protection to every pump on board.
It says the starter needs an overload but not where it sits or what to set it to, which is the first thing he would set on a job, so add one line if research can source it.
Only small-motor limits are given, so nothing shows that a strong supply starts much bigger motors DOL, and the brief's ABB 250 kW line should be quoted and added if research can find it.
The card has no fault rule of thumb, so add the one he would use most: 'Runs only while Start is held: check 7. Will not start: check the overload first.'
Footnote [^13] sits on the definition of no-volt protection, which he already knows, so drop it.

It reads as a build spec ('Nine screens, with Back and Continue', 'in the app's style', 'marked in amber', 'may wrap onto two rows on a phone'), and the Book prints it under 'What you're looking at' when the chapter has a plate, so rewrite it as a short plain description of the drawing or make sure it is not shown.
